mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE stays below 4% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of episodes meeting the INDPRO contraction trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals a broad-based demand collapse, which amplifies recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1.0% AND HOUST monthly change < -1.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from baseline during episodes where both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 1% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive easing cycle that boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during episodes where FEDFUNDS falls below 1% in a recession (UNRATE > 5%).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of sustained above-trend PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts central bank tightening and reduces corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > 3.0% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during episodes of sustained high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% for six months).
